work_division_v1.scene: After a handoff, the same machine sounds an alarm for three days in a row. Repeating that day's operating sequence can connect the questions raised by the logs to what the machine actually does. When you can link those two parts of the work, you can test the proposed fix on site.
work_division_v1.tradeoff: A role responsible for restoring operations can close the issue once the fault is fixed. A role investigating the cause also needs to leave evidence someone else can check. The distinction is who has time to reproduce the problem as well as who does the hands-on work.
work_division_v1.question: The last time a machine went back into operation and then sounded the same alarm, what did this role handle? Who could schedule a retest?

work_division_v1.scene: Imagine building displays for a pop-up exhibition that must come apart and go back together. The sketch determines what visitors see first. A trial assembly shows whether the pieces are easy to carry and whether the seams draw attention. Adjusting the joints or the shape could get you closer to the look you want.
work_division_v1.tradeoff: If the design is already final, your job is mainly to build a finished display that goes together. Joining at the prototype stage can give you room to change the structure or presentation. It also means allowing time for experimentation, rework, and on-site constraints.
work_division_v1.question: Could you describe a time when a trial assembly led to a design change? What could the fabrication team change on its own, and what needed the designer's approval?

work_division_v1.scene: A city transportation study finds that the people taking the longest detours are already familiar with the roads. First compare records for different routes to see how reliable the finding is. Then decide whether a map, a chart, or prose would best help readers see where the detours occur.
work_division_v1.tradeoff: Writing a research conclusion that someone can trace back to the evidence takes a different kind of attention from creating a piece readers can follow. Some roles receive conclusions that are already final. If you want to do both, ask whether you can see the original materials.
work_division_v1.question: Could you show me something the team delivered recently? Which evidence did the person in this role look at, and which decisions did they make about how to present it?
